recommendations.title: Explore your career goal
recommendations.text: Learn about the degrees and careers you could aim for. Your teachers and the school career guidance unit can help you choose a goal that fits you.
recommendations.reason: You said you did not have a clear career goal yet (No).
evidence: Model: the Phase 8 explanation found this group of answers linked to the Z-score (a pattern, not proof)
Research: Specific goals direct effort (Locke & Latham, 2002)

recommendations.title: Strengthen your Science basics early
recommendations.text: Spend extra time on the basics of Science at the start of A/L, before new topics build on them. Ask your teacher which O/L topics matter most for your A/L subjects.
recommendations.reason: Your O/L Science grade was C, and Medicine needs strong Science.
evidence: Model: the Phase 8 explanation found this group of answers linked to the Z-score (a pattern, not proof)

recommendations.title: Build confidence step by step
recommendations.text: Start each topic with easier questions, then move to harder ones. Keep a list of the topics you have mastered and add to it every week.
recommendations.reason: Your answers about confidence in your studies were in the middle or lower part of the scale.
evidence: Model: the Phase 8 explanation found this group of answers linked to the Z-score (a pattern, not proof)
Research: Mastery experiences build self-efficacy (Bandura, 1997)

recommendations.title: Make a simple weekly timetable
recommendations.text: Write a weekly timetable with short, fixed study blocks (for example 45 minutes), and tick each block when you finish it. Small blocks are easier to keep than long ones.
recommendations.reason: You said it was often hard to stick to a study schedule.
evidence: Model: the Phase 8 explanation found this group of answers linked to the Z-score (a pattern, not proof)
Research: Effort regulation and self-regulated learning (Pintrich et al., 1991; Zimmerman, 2002)

recommendations.title: Connect your subjects to your goal
recommendations.text: Find out how the Science and Maths you learn are used in Medicine. Short videos, books or talking to someone who studies it can make the subjects more interesting.
recommendations.reason: Your answers about interest in Science and Maths were in the middle or lower part of the scale.
evidence: Model: the Phase 8 explanation found this group of answers linked to the Z-score (a pattern, not proof)
Research: Interest development (Hidi & Renninger, 2006)

recommendations.title: Give every study session one clear goal
recommendations.text: Before you start, write one small goal for the session, such as "finish 10 Chemistry MCQs" or "summarise one Physics lesson". Check it at the end.
recommendations.reason: You said you did not always make good use of your study time.
evidence: Model: the Phase 8 explanation found this group of answers linked to the Z-score (a pattern, not proof)
Research: Goal setting (Locke & Latham, 2002)

recommendations.title: Do a weekly catch-up
recommendations.text: Keep one fixed time each weekend to go over the week's lessons and finish any homework that is left, so work does not pile up.
recommendations.reason: You said you did not always keep up with schoolwork every week.
evidence: Model: the Phase 8 explanation found this group of answers linked to the Z-score (a pattern, not proof)
Research: Spaced practice (Dunlosky et al., 2013)

recommendations.title: Practise past papers
recommendations.text: After you finish a topic, practise past paper questions on it. Most similar students who reached Medicine practised past papers "Weekly" during A/L.
recommendations.reason: This is what similar successful students in our survey reported doing.
evidence: Survey: what similar students who reached this target reported
Research: Practice testing (Roediger & Karpicke, 2006; Dunlosky et al., 2013)

recommendations.title: Revise earlier lessons regularly
recommendations.text: Go back to lessons from earlier weeks and months, not only the newest ones. Most similar students who reached Medicine revised earlier work "Often".
recommendations.reason: This is what similar successful students in our survey reported doing.
evidence: Survey: what similar students who reached this target reported
Research: Distributed practice (Dunlosky et al., 2013)

recommendations.title: Also keep backup options in mind
recommendations.text: While you work towards Medicine, also look at degree areas your predicted Z-score already reaches in your district: Allied Health Sciences, Agriculture or Food Science, Biological Science.
recommendations.reason: Your predicted Z-score is 0.76 below the lowest Medicine cut-off in your district.
evidence: Official: UGC minimum Z-score documents

recommendations.title: Set a weekly self-study target
recommendations.text: Plan your own study time every week, on top of school and tuition. Students like you who reached Medicine studied regularly, on most days of the week, during A/L. Build up your own study time step by step, and keep time for sleep, rest and family.
recommendations.reason: Your Grade 11 self-study time (Less than 5 hours a week) was lower than that of most similar students who reached Medicine.
